title: R’ Chanina or Chananyah, son of R’ Yose the Galilean

paragraphs: R’ Chanina (or Chananyah), son of R’ Yose the Galilean. (Tanna).

Hyman describes him as the leading sage of his generation in Usha’s Sanhedrin under the presidency of R’ Shimon ben Gamliel. [Rosh Hashanah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.32a.13-15) relates that when the court sanctified the year at Usha, R’ Yochanan ben Beroka went down before R’ Shimon ben Gamliel. On the second day, R’ Chanina, son of R’ Yose the Galilean, went down and acted according to R’ Akiva, etc. [Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 6:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.6.8.10), [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.2.30), and [Sifra, Emor](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra%2C_Emor%2C_Section_11.5) (Hyman’s section 178), have R’ Chananyah son of R’ Yose the Galilean. He is also mentioned in [Chullin 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.12a.11), disputing with R’ Yehudah about one whose kids and chickens were lost and who went and found them slaughtered.

The statement is also brought in [Bava Metzia 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.24b.9-10) and [Tosefta Chullin 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Chullin.2.2), where Hyman gives the reading Chanina.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. II, p. 492](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=75) cites Rosh Hashanah 31b. The matching 32a passage gives Yochanan ben Beroka first; the Jerusalem Talmud gives his son Yishmael and the Sifra gives his son Shimon. Rav Chisda takes the “second day” in Rosh Hashanah to mean the following year. Chullin has Chanina in the ruling; the consulted Bava Metzia and Tosefta have Chananyah. In the Tosefta he disqualifies the animal in a theft case. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1453&lang=en) collects the name forms and several of these parallels.
